mainTopic: Who may perform שחיטה, and whether the משנה's word הכל means a person may slaughter לכתחלה or only that the שחיטה is valid בדיעבד
overview: The משנה opens מסכת חולין by teaching that everyone may slaughter, except a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן, because they might ruin the שחיטה. Even they have a valid שחיטה if others watch them. The גמרא notices a contradiction in the משנה's first line: 'הכל שוחטין' sounds like לכתחלה, but 'ושחיטתן כשרה' sounds like only דיעבד. רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges the idea that 'הכל' always means לכתחלה, pointing to 'הכל ממירין' in תמורה, even though the תורה forbids making a תמורה. The answer is that the תמורה משנה itself says it is only בדיעבד, and our משנה says nothing like that. רב אחא then brings 'הכל מעריכין' from ערכין, where there is no such limit, even though פסוקים in דברים and קהלת show that vowing is not ideal. He adds a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר says it is best not to vow at all, while רבי יהודה praises one who vows and pays. רב אחא then shows that even רבי יהודה praises only a vow of 'הרי זו', and this point continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Everyone may slaughter, except three groups
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that everyone may slaughter and the שחיטה is valid, except a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן, who might ruin it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone may slaughter, and their slaughter is valid. The exceptions are a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person and a minor, because they might ruin their slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens מסכת חולין with the basic rule of who may perform שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is wide: 'everyone.' Three groups are left out, and the reason is practical. They may not know how to do the שחיטה properly and could make it invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Kosher slaughter of an animal
A deaf-mute, considered not legally competent
A mentally incompetent person
A minor, not yet of age

phrases.english: MISHNA: Everyone slaughters
and their slaughter is valid,
except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
lest they ruin their slaughter.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone may slaughter and the slaughter is valid, except a חרש, שוטה and קטן, who might ruin it.

steps.title: Supervised slaughter by the excluded groups is valid
steps.stepSummary: If a חרש, שוטה or קטן slaughters while others watch, the שחיטה is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of these, if they slaughtered while others were watching them, their slaughter is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that even the three excluded groups can have a valid שחיטה if someone supervises them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their problem was only the worry that they might ruin the שחיטה. When competent people watch and see it was done properly, that worry is gone, so the שחיטה is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Others are watching them, meaning supervision

steps.whatToRemember: The exclusion of חרש, שוטה and קטן is about the risk of a mistake. Supervision removes that risk.

phrases.english: And for all of them, when they slaughtered
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the three groups just left out: חרש, שוטה and קטן.

phrases.english: and others see them,
their slaughter is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the exclusion in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרש, שוטה or קטן who slaughters under supervision has a valid שחיטה.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that 'הכל שוחטין' sounds like לכתחלה, while 'ושחיטתן כשרה' sounds like only דיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone slaughters' implies it is allowed from the start. But 'and their slaughter is valid' implies it is only valid after the fact!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by pointing out that two phrases in the משנה's first line seem to say different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Everyone slaughters' sounds like permission to slaughter in the first place (לכתחלה). 'Their slaughter is valid' sounds like it already happened and we only judge the result (דיעבד). You can't have both, so which does the משנה mean?

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
From the start: permitted to do in the first place
After the fact: valid once done, though not ideal

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the שחיטה works. It's whether a person may slaughter in the first place, or whether we only accept it once it's done.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between לכתחלה and דיעבד shapes the whole opening of the מסכת. It tells us whether a regular person may slaughter on his own or only that his שחיטה is accepted afterwards.

phrases.english: GEMARA: 'Everyone slaughters' means ab initio,
'and their slaughter is valid' means after the fact!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל שׁוֹחֲטִין לְכַתְּחִלָּה וּשְׁחִיטָתָן כְּשֵׁרָה דִּיעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the wording of the משנה's opening line
steps.kashyaTarget: The opening line of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two phrases of the same sentence seem to point to two different levels of permission, לכתחלה and דיעבד.

steps.title: Does 'הכל' always mean permitted from the start?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי whether 'הכל' really means לכתחלה, pointing to 'הכל ממירין' in תמורה, which cannot be permitted because the תורה forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: Does every 'everyone' mean ab initio? If so, 'everyone can substitute, men and women alike': is that also ab initio? But it is written: 'He shall not exchange it nor substitute it, good for bad or bad for good'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא challenges the assumption behind step 3, that the word 'הכל' means לכתחלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in תמורה also says 'הכל ממירין,' yet the תורה clearly forbids making a תמורה. So 'הכל' there can't mean it is allowed from the start. If so, maybe 'הכל' here doesn't mean לכתחלה either, and the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Trying to swap a regular animal into the place of a קרבן animal; both become holy
They make a תמורה, they substitute
If that is so then: a challenge showing a strange result
Is that also so?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
And does every 'everyone' mean ab initio?
If that is so: 'Everyone substitutes,'
phrases.notes: This is quoting the first משנה of מסכת תמורה.

phrases.english: both men and women:
is that also ab initio?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כְּתִיב: ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אֹתוֹ
phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'He shall neither exchange it, nor substitute it,
good for bad, or bad for good'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the premise of the question in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the word 'הכל' means לכתחלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In תמורה the משנה says 'הכל ממירין' about something the תורה forbids, so 'הכל' cannot always mean permitted from the start.

steps.title: In תמורה the משנה says outright that it is only after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in תמורה the משנה itself explains that a person may not substitute, only that if he does, it takes effect and he gets מלקות. Our משנה has no such limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it explains its reason: not that a person is permitted to substitute, but that if he did substitute, it takes effect and he receives the forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the reading that 'הכל' means לכתחלה by showing why the תמורה case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in תמורה adds its own explanation that 'הכל' there is only בדיעבד, since doing it is a sin punished by מלקות. Without such an explanation, 'הכל' means לכתחלה. Our משנה gives no such explanation, so 'הכל שוחטין' still means לכתחלה, and the contradiction from step 3 is back.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in the other case
Permitted
Here: the swap takes effect and the new animal becomes holy
Receives the forty lashes (מלקות)

steps.confusionAlert: 'מומר' here has nothing to do with a person who abandons the תורה. It just means the substitution worked.
steps.whatToRemember: 'הכל' normally means לכתחלה unless the משנה itself says otherwise, as in תמורה. So the question of step 3 still needs an answer.

phrases.english: There, as it teaches the reason:
not that a person is permitted to substitute,
but that if he did substitute, the substitution takes effect,
and he incurs the forty lashes.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the other משנה explicitly limits its own wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'הכל ממירין' is only בדיעבד, maybe 'הכל' never means לכתחלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הכל' in תמורה is only בדיעבד because that משנה says so. Without such a limit, 'הכל' means לכתחלה, so the question on our משנה remains.

steps.title: Second challenge: everyone may vow, but vowing is not ideal
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא brings the משנה in ערכין, 'הכל מעריכין ונערכין, נודרין ונידרין', and asks whether 'הכל' there also means לכתחלה, since a פסוק says it is better not to vow at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the משנה that says 'Everyone may make valuation vows and be valuated, may vow and be vowed'? Does that also mean it is fine to do so from the start? But the פסוק says: 'If you hold back from vowing, there will be no sin in you'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא brings a second example of a משנה that starts with 'הכל' even though the act is not ideal. This supports his point that 'הכל שוחטין' in our משנה does not have to mean לכתחלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תמורה example was just answered because that משנה limits itself. So רב אחא brings a new 'הכל' משנה in ערכין that has no such limit. Since the תורה praises someone who does not vow, 'הכל נודרין' cannot mean that vowing is ideal. That shows 'הכל' can mean 'it works if done', not 'go ahead and do it'.

keyTerms.meaning: Valuation vows. Someone promises to give the בית המקדש the fixed amount the תורה sets for a person, based on age and gender.
Make a valuation vow, and be the person whose value is pledged.
Vow to give a person's market value, and be the person whose market value is pledged.
Hold back from vowing.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of pledges. In ערכין the amount is fixed by the תורה, while in נודרין the amount is what the person would sell for in the market.

phrases.english: But [the משנה says]: Everyone may pledge valuations and be valuated,
may vow [a person's worth] and have their worth vowed,
is that also meant as allowed from the start?
But it is written:
"And if you hold back from vowing,
there will be no sin in you"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תמורה example was answered, רב אחא brings a new 'הכל' משנה that does not limit itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The defense in step 5 that 'הכל' without any limit in the משנה means לכתחלה, which is what makes 'הכל שוחטין' read as לכתחלה in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'הכל נודרין' cannot mean vowing is ideal, because the תורה praises not vowing. So 'הכל' does not have to mean לכתחלה.

steps.title: More support: a פסוק in קהלת and a ברייתא about vowing
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא adds a פסוק from קהלת and a ברייתא. רבי מאיר says it is best never to vow. רבי יהודה says it is best to vow and pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'It is better not to vow than to vow and not pay.' And a ברייתא teaches: Better than both of these is someone who does not vow at all. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: Better than both of these is someone who vows and pays.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא strengthens his point with a second פסוק and a ברייתא showing that vowing is not seen as ideal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads the פסוק as saying the best path is not to vow at all, which fits רב אחא's point. רבי יהודה seems to disagree, since he praises a person who vows and pays. The next step deals with that.

keyTerms.meaning: Better than both this one and that one.
At all.
Vows and then pays (keeps the vow).

phrases.english: And it is written: "It is better that you not vow
than that you vow and not pay",
and a ברייתא teaches: Better than this one and that one
phrases.notes: 'This one and that one' means the person who vows and pays, and the person who vows and doesn't pay.

phrases.english: is one who does not vow at all,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: טוֹב מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: Better than this one and that one
phrases.notes: For רבי יהודה, 'this one and that one' means the person who doesn't vow at all, and the person who vows and doesn't pay.

phrases.english: is one who vows and pays.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: ״טוֹב אֲשֶׁר לֹא תִדֹּר מִשֶּׁתִּדּוֹר וְלֹא תְשַׁלֵּם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק and a ברייתא to back up the claim that vowing is not ideal.
steps.raayaObject: That vowing is not ideal, so 'הכל נודרין' cannot mean לכתחלה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in קהלת 5:4 and the ברייתא of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה praises vowing only in a limited case
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא points out that even רבי יהודה only praises vowing when someone says 'הרי זו', which sets aside a specific item.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רבי יהודה only said this when a person says 'This one is [a קרבן]'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא blocks a possible answer: someone might say the ערכין משנה follows רבי יהודה, who likes vowing. He shows that רבי יהודה's praise is narrow. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'הרי זו' ties the vow to one specific item that is already set aside, so there is little risk of failing to keep it. A general pledge, like a valuation vow, is not that case. So even by רבי יהודה, 'הכל מעריכין' is not לכתחלה, and רב אחא's challenge stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This one is [a קרבן]', a vow pointing at a specific item.
He only said it in the case of.

phrases.english: And even רבי יהודה only said [this]
in the case of one who says "This one is [a קרבן]",

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קָאָמַר אֶלָּא בְּאוֹמֵר ״הֲרֵי זוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי יהודה's view from step 7 so it cannot be used to defend reading 'הכל' as לכתחלה.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible defense that the ערכין משנה follows רבי יהודה and so means לכתחלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה praises vowing only when the vow is tied to a specific item ('הרי זו'), not general pledges like ערכין. So the challenge stands even by his view.
